title: Vividness and Concrete Language
description: Specific, picture-making language persuades far more than abstract statistics.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: A single concrete detail — a name, an image, a small scene — moves people more than an accurate statistic. The mind remembers and acts on what it can picture.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Concrete language is easier to encode and to imagine, and imagined events feel more real. Statistics require effortful processing; images arrive ready-made.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: "One in five children" versus "a girl in your daughter's class" — the second lands harder.
A charity appeal naming one person outperforms a report about millions.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: A story used where a figure would be more accurate.
Details you can see, smell or hear.

sections.title: Ethical Uses
sections.content: Use a concrete example to make a real statistic meaningful — pair the story with the evidence.

sections.title: Manipulative Uses
sections.content: Replacing representative evidence with a single vivid case that is not typical.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: An emotional story offered as if it were proof.
A dramatic example standing in for the base rate.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Ask how typical the vivid example is.
Keep the statistic alongside the story.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Letting a memorable case outweigh the data.
Assuming you are unmoved by imagery.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Vivid cases are memorable but not representative.
